provenance.head: 4a9a3070b09f2a68ee2fcbe4ace51cb107c72f61
provenance.nim: Nim Compiler Version 2.3.1 [Linux: amd64] (codetracer-nim fork, from the dev shell)
provenance.host: 32 logical cores, shared CI runner. Every compile-cost and footprint figure here was taken in one window at load average 65-95. The mutation runs later in the session ran at load 200-300 and contribute no cost figure — only exit codes and per-case verdicts, which load does not move.
provenance.costMetric: CPU seconds (ru_utime+ru_stime of the waited-for child tree, via os.wait4). Wall time is recorded per compile but is NOT comparable across the campaign: the host carried 65-95 load from other users throughout.
provenance.runMetric: TWO run figures per binary, because they answer different questions and only one of them is comparable to batch 1. `perCaseWarm*` is one process per case, `--run "suite::test"`, two passes, the second reported — the shape the M3 runner uses, and the only shape in which a bundle pays its module init once per case. `wholeBinaryWarm*` is the binary run with no arguments, two passes, second reported. Batch 1's `warmRun*` is the per-case shape; compare against `perCaseWarm*`.
provenance.note: Every binary here was compiled fresh into a private nimcache under TMPDIR. No figure is read back out of a pre-existing artifact, and none is carried forward from batch 1 — including the two batch-1 bundles, which this batch rebuilt only so the verification test could run against them and did not re-record.

limits.rationale: See `MaxBundleMembers` in scripts/generate_test_edges.nim. 24 remains a ceiling on what may be ATTEMPTED, not a certificate that 24 is safe: the from-source recipe family failed merged at 24 and passed at 16. This batch's largest bundle is 13. Every bundle here shows per-case pass under --run plus whole-binary exit 0 on its own evidence.
limits.enforcementPoints: maxBundleMembers and maxBundleOwners are enforced in the generator by `checkBundleLimits`, which quits(1) rather than warns. maxDependencyRoots is asserted from this ledger ONLY; the generator has no corresponding constant. Batch 1's brief mis-stated this and its ledger recorded `dependencyShape: []` for ONE of its two bundles (bundle_repro_lock_files_pure_unit; bundle_repro_peer_cache_pure_unit correctly records ['repro_peer_cache']), which made the ledger-side assertion vacuous for that one bundle — this batch records the real group shapes (1, 1, 2, 1 roots). CORRECTED AT REVIEW: this field previously said `[]` for BOTH batch-1 bundles, which the file at a7798b480 refutes.

compatibilityAliasesNote: FOUR ENTRIES, ONE HONEST RENAME, and it is in libs/repro_dsl_stdlib/tests/t_packaging_wrapper_vars_match_flake.nim. The `--set-default` wrapper loop this suite guards moved out of flake.nix into nix/pkgs/by-name/re/reprobuild/package.nix, so the suite name `packaging: the §5 wrapper-var list tracks flake.nix` had stopped being true and the case `flake.nix still has a recognisable wrapProgram contract` named a file that no longer carries the contract. Restoring either name so this ledger's selectors keep resolving would have written a false statement back into the source to quiet a checker, which is the inverse of what the checker is for. Each entry maps one selector THIS ledger recorded from the member's own standalone binary to the `suite::test` selector that addresses the same case today; both halves are fully qualified, so the suite rename is DECLARED here rather than inferred anywhere. NOT A RESTATED MEASUREMENT: the `bundles`, `suite` and `limits` blocks are untouched and still say what was measured when this batch landed. This field is the one part of a landed ledger that is a decision rather than a measurement, and it has to be able to grow -- a redirection table frozen at the moment of landing could never redirect anything. The entries are load-bearing in both directions: tests/integration/t_m4_pure_unit_consolidation.nim goes red if an entry's target names no case in the bundle, and red again if an entry matches no selector any ledger records.

suite.binariesAddedByThisBatchNote: Zero, and stated rather than omitted. Batch 1 brought tests/integration/t_m4_pure_unit_consolidation.nim with it and its suite-wide fall was therefore smaller than the number consolidation removed; this batch adds no binary, so the fall of 18 is exactly the 22 members minus the 4 bundles that replaced them.
suite.testEntriesNote: Nim + Python. The Python half (8 entries) is untouched by this batch.
suite.staticCaseSumNote: UNCHANGED. Consolidation contributes zero static cases and this batch adds no test of its own, so unlike batch 1 (+3, its own verification test) there is nothing to attribute. Sum over scripts/reprobuild-suite-static-case-counts.tsv, regenerated by --write-static-case-counts.
suite.consolidationGroupsNote: -4 consumed by this batch, +2 NEW groups whose members are themselves bundles: (tests/bundles, ['repro_lock_files']) pairs bundle_repro_lock_files_pure_unit with bundle_repro_lock_files_cli_pure_unit, and (tests/bundles, ['repro_core']) pairs the two repro_core bundles. Those two are not actionable candidates: checkBundleLimits refuses any member under tests/bundles by construction. The candidate list does not know that, which is a defect in the candidate list rather than in the limit.

staticCrossCheckCorrection.what: test_consolidation_reduces_binary_footprint used to assert `staticTotal == enumerated`: the Python source scan's count of a bundle against the built binary's own --list-json catalog.
staticCrossCheckCorrection.whyItWasWrong: That equality is false in general and the static table's own header says so — the scan sums every when/else branch. libs/repro_core/tests/t_smoke_repro_core.nim has six cases under `when defined(windows)` and one under `else`, so the scan counts 14 where a Linux binary enumerates 8, and bundle_repro_core_pure_unit went red at 69 vs 63 the first time the verification test ran against this batch. None of batch 1's 21 members was platform-conditional, so the assertion had never been exercised.
staticCrossCheckCorrection.whatItIsNow: The scanner's count of the BUNDLE must equal the scanner's count of the MEMBERS, summed, from each member's `staticCaseCountAtBase` recorded here. The platform over-count is a property of the member sources and survives the move unchanged, so it cancels on both sides; a deleted `test` block does not. Ledgers without per-member static counts (batch 1) keep the assertion they shipped with, unrelaxed.
staticCrossCheckCorrection.whyThisIsNotAWeakening: The old form did not catch a deletion at all: deleting a `test` moved static and enumerated together and left the equality green (demonstrated by M2-static, where the old form would have passed). The new form makes the two producers independent, which is what the verification file's header always claimed.
staticCrossCheckCorrection.otherCorrection: `check declaredSources.len >= after` was anchored to batch 1's nimTestBinariesAfter on the reasoning that the count only ever grows. It does not: this batch made it fall from 1512 to 1494 against a recorded 1510. It is now anchored to the NEWEST ledger's `after`, the only one that is a lower bound.

defectFoundAndFixedAtReview.what: The verification test pinned the bundles to the ledger with `==` on case counts and on the extra-case set. The ledger is a DATED record that is never rewritten, so the first time anyone adds a case to a consolidated member source the file goes red permanently, for a reason the author of the addition did not cause and cannot fix without falsifying a measurement.
defectFoundAndFixedAtReview.itWasNotHypothetical: Merging origin/dev turned it red: exit 1 with four failed assertions (extra.len == 0; enumerated == recorded; staticTotal == staticFromMembers; casesAfter == casesBefore). Three unrelated packaging commits (ea73d993b, b3d6117d0, 937cd66ad) had added seven `test` blocks to libs/repro_dsl_stdlib/tests/t_packaging_wrapper_vars_match_flake.nim, a member of bundle_repro_dsl_stdlib_catalogs_pure_unit. Fourteen commits was all it took.
defectFoundAndFixedAtReview.fix: missing.len == 0 is UNCHANGED and exact — it is the loss detector and it works by name. `extra.len == 0` becomes attribution: every extra case must come from a `file` the bundle's ledger entry lists as a member, which keeps the power that check actually had (a member added to PureUnitBundles and written into no ledger cannot pass) while tolerating a case added to a known member. The three count comparisons become >=: a fall is a loss and stays red, a rise is the repository working.
defectFoundAndFixedAtReview.whyThisIsNotAWeakening: Every loss is still caught, and by name rather than by count. The mutation campaign below re-runs on the merged tree and shows it: M1 (a deleted case) red, M2-static (deleted in source, table regenerated, binary stale) red on the static arm alone, M3 (a renamed suite at unchanged count) red on cases 1 and 3 with case 2 green, M-attrib (a member in the generator that no ledger names) red on the attribution check. M-grow is the control that makes the fix meaningful rather than merely quiet: a case ADDED to a member, bundle rebuilt, static table regenerated — green.
